easy.question: Where did all the children of Israel assemble according to the verse?
answers: Shiloh
Gilgal
Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The verse begins 'And the whole congregation... at Shiloh' — it states they assembled at Shiloh.

easy.question: What did the children of Israel set up there according to the verse?
answers: An altar
The tabernacle of the congregation
A military fortress
easy.explanation: The verse says they 'set up the tabernacle of the congregation' — they placed the tabernacle there.

easy.question: What is said about the land in the verse?
answers: It became fruitful
It had been subdued before them
It remained unconquered
easy.explanation: The verse notes 'And the land was subdued before them' — the land had been brought under their control.

medium.question: Why is it likely the tabernacle was set up at Shiloh?
answers: So it would be a central cultic and communal center for Israel
To make Shiloh a political capital
To conceal a military command
medium.explanation: The tabernacle is the meeting and worship place; placing it at Shiloh implies it was chosen as a religious center.

medium.question: In the phrase 'the land was subdued before them,' what does 'was subdued' mean in context?
answers: It means the land was conquered or brought under their control
It became fertile and prosperous
It was completely destroyed
medium.explanation: 'Was subdued' here means it was taken or brought under control by the people; context indicates conquest before their settlement.

medium.question: What can be inferred from the sequence: assembly at Shiloh and then setting up the tabernacle?
answers: They performed a battle ritual there
Shiloh was chosen as a central place for Israel
The tabernacle was only a temporary structure for soldiers
medium.explanation: The gathering followed by installing the tabernacle suggests Shiloh was chosen as a central place for worship and communal life.

challenge.question: In the phrase 'the land was subdued before them', what does 'before them' imply about the timing of the event?
answers: That the conquest will happen in the near future
That the conquest is unrelated to Israel
That the land was subdued by the Israelites before they settled at Shiloh
challenge.explanation: 'Before them' indicates the land had been subdued prior to or as they advanced — i.e., the people had conquered it before establishing the religious center at Shiloh.

challenge.question: What importance of Shiloh in Israelite history is already visible in this verse?
answers: Its establishment as a cultic center during the entry into the land and the period of the Judges
Being the capital of the united monarchy of Israel
Being the birthplace of Joshua
challenge.explanation: Setting the tabernacle at Shiloh and the assembly there point to its role as a religious center after the conquests.

challenge.question: How do the verbs 'assembled' and 'set up' relate to the significance of the action in the verse?
answers: They both describe only military and guarding actions
They show a sequence: first assembly, then establishing the tabernacle as an institutional act
They both describe a single action of moving from place to place
challenge.explanation: 'Assembled' — they gathered; 'set up' — they placed the tabernacle. The sequence implies gathering followed by establishing a worship center.

answers: That the conquest will happen in the near future
That the conquest is unrelated to Israel
That the land was subdued by the Israelites before they settled at Shiloh
questions.explanation: 'Before them' indicates the land had been subdued prior to or as they advanced — i.e., the people had conquered it before establishing the religious center at Shiloh.

Being the capital of the united monarchy of Israel
Being the birthplace of Joshua
questions.explanation: Setting the tabernacle at Shiloh and the assembly there point to its role as a religious center after the conquests.

paragraphs.title: Tribes Without Inheritance and Joshua's Rebuke

easy.question: What does verse 2 say remained among the children of Israel?
answers: Seven tribes
Three tribes
All tribes received an inheritance
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly states 'seven tribes' remained without division of their inheritance.

easy.question: Who speaks to the children of Israel in verse 3?
answers: Moses
Joshua
The elders of the people
easy.explanation: The verse begins 'And Joshua said unto the children of Israel' — Joshua is speaking.

easy.question: What does Joshua demand the people to do in verse 3?
answers: Pray for the land
Wait for further instructions
Go possess the land
easy.explanation: Joshua asks 'How long are ye slack to go to possess the land' — he urges them to go and take possession.

medium.question: What does the phrase 'which had not yet received their inheritance' mean in verse 2?
answers: They had already divided their inheritance
They still had not received or divided their portion in the land
They gave their inheritance to other tribes
medium.explanation: The wording indicates those tribes had not yet received their portions — they were still awaiting allotment.

medium.question: In the phrase 'How long are ye slack to go to possess the land,' what does 'slack' mean in context? (context phrase: "How long are ye slack")
answers: Excessive rest
Growing weak/hesitating and failing to act
Remaining on alert
medium.explanation: 'Slack' here means weakened or delayed from acting; Joshua's question chides their inactivity and hesitation to take their inheritance.

medium.question: According to the verse, who is the giver of the land to Israel?
answers: The Lord God of your fathers
Joshua himself
The other tribes
medium.explanation: The verse states 'which the Lord God of your fathers hath given you' — the land was given by God.

challenge.question: What is Joshua's rhetorical intent in the question 'How long are ye slack'?
answers: He is neutrally asking about the timing of the division
It is a literal punishment marking the end of settlement
He is rebuking and urging immediate action
challenge.explanation: The question has a rebuking tone meant to spur them to act — Joshua criticizes their slackness and demands immediate possession.

challenge.question: Why is it historically plausible that only seven tribes remained without an inheritance at this point?
answers: Because some tribes had already received an inheritance, leaving seven yet to receive theirs
Because seven tribes were condemned to wander in the desert
Because seven tribes were exempt from receiving land
challenge.explanation: The context implies that other tribes had already been allotted land, so seven remained to be assigned.

challenge.question: What is the precise sense of the verb 'to possess' in 'go to possess the land'?
answers: To negotiate for the land
To take and inherit the land as their portion
To leave the land for someone else
challenge.explanation: 'To possess' means to take ownership or receive an inheritance; here it refers to securing land allotments as hereditary possession.

questions.question: What is Joshua's rhetorical intent in the question 'How long are ye slack'?
answers: He is neutrally asking about the timing of the division
It is a literal punishment marking the end of settlement
He is rebuking and urging immediate action
questions.explanation: The question has a rebuking tone meant to spur them to act — Joshua criticizes their slackness and demands immediate possession.

questions.question: Why is it historically plausible that only seven tribes remained without an inheritance at this point?
answers: Because some tribes had already received an inheritance, leaving seven yet to receive theirs
Because seven tribes were condemned to wander in the desert
Because seven tribes were exempt from receiving land
questions.explanation: The context implies that other tribes had already been allotted land, so seven remained to be assigned.

questions.question: What is the precise sense of the verb 'to possess' in 'go to possess the land'?
answers: To negotiate for the land
To take and inherit the land as their portion
To leave the land for someone else
questions.explanation: 'To possess' means to take ownership or receive an inheritance; here it refers to securing land allotments as hereditary possession.

paragraphs.title: Sending Surveyors and Reminder about the Levites

easy.question: How many men did he send from each tribe according to the verse?
answers: Three
One
Seven
easy.explanation: Verse 4 says 'Give out from among you three men for each tribe' — three men per tribe.

easy.question: What were those men instructed to do in the land according to the verse?
answers: Fight its inhabitants
Go through the land and describe it
Build dwelling places there
easy.explanation: The verse instructs them 'and they shall rise, and go through the land, and describe it' — to survey and record the land.

easy.question: After surveying, into how many parts were they told to divide the land?
answers: Twelve
Five
Seven
easy.explanation: Verse 5 states 'they shall divide it into seven parts' — seven divisions.

medium.question: Who was assigned the southern coast according to the verse?
answers: Judah
The house of Joseph
The Levites
medium.explanation: Verse 5 says 'Judah shall abide in their coast on the south' — Judah holds the southern boundary.

medium.question: What does Joshua mean by 'I will cast lots for you here before the Lord' (phrase: 'cast lots')?
answers: A combat tool
An impartial method of decision by lot for allotment
A place-name
medium.explanation: Here 'cast lots' refers to the ritual of deciding allotments by lot; the context 'before the Lord' makes it a solemn, divinely acknowledged method.

medium.question: Why did they bring the written descriptions of the land to Joshua?
answers: So he would oversee construction
So he could cast lots and allot the inheritances before the Lord
So he could impose taxes
medium.explanation: Verse 6 indicates they brought the descriptions so Joshua could cast lots before the Lord and divide the land.

challenge.question: Why do the Levites have no portion among the tribes according to the verse?
answers: Because the priesthood of the Lord is their inheritance
Because they were exiled outside the land
Because they already received extensive lands
challenge.explanation: Verse 7 states 'the Levites have no part among you; for the priesthood of the Lord is their inheritance' — their role and priesthood are considered their portion.

challenge.question: Which tribes had already received their inheritance beyond the Jordan according to verse 7?
answers: Judah and Levi
Half of Manasseh only
Gad, Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh
challenge.explanation: Verse 7 lists 'Gad, and Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh' as those who received their portions east of Jordan.

challenge.question: Why did they divide the land into seven parts (inferred from the chapter context)?
answers: Because seven is a random number with no relation to the tribes
Because seven regions/tribes still needed allotment within the western land
To preserve seven cultic centers
challenge.explanation: Given some tribes already had eastern allotments and the Levites had none, seven divisions remained to be allotted within the west, matching the remaining groups.

questions.question: Why do the Levites have no portion among the tribes according to the verse?
answers: Because the priesthood of the Lord is their inheritance
Because they were exiled outside the land
Because they already received extensive lands
questions.explanation: Verse 7 states 'the Levites have no part among you; for the priesthood of the Lord is their inheritance' — their role and priesthood are considered their portion.

questions.question: Which tribes had already received their inheritance beyond the Jordan according to verse 7?
answers: Judah and Levi
Half of Manasseh only
Gad, Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh
questions.explanation: Verse 7 lists 'Gad, and Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh' as those who received their portions east of Jordan.

questions.question: Why did they divide the land into seven parts (inferred from the chapter context)?
answers: Because seven is a random number with no relation to the tribes
Because seven regions/tribes still needed allotment within the western land
To preserve seven cultic centers
questions.explanation: Given some tribes already had eastern allotments and the Levites had none, seven divisions remained to be allotted within the west, matching the remaining groups.

easy.question: What did Joshua command the men who went to survey the land to do?
answers: Walk through the land and describe it
Keep camp and light fires
Travel to Jerusalem and build an altar
easy.explanation: Joshua charged them to 'Go and walk through the land, and describe it' — to survey and record it.

easy.question: Where did the men return after they wrote the description of the land?
answers: To Mount Carmel
To the great sea
To Joshua at the camp in Shiloh
easy.explanation: The verse states they 'came again to Joshua to the host at Shiloh' — they returned to Shiloh.

easy.question: Into how many parts did they write the land by cities?
answers: Three
Seven
Ten
easy.explanation: They described the land 'by cities into seven parts' — seven divisions.

medium.question: Why did they write and bring the land description to Joshua before he cast lots?
answers: So Joshua could oversee building projects
So he could cast lots and allot the inheritances
So they could sell the cities
medium.explanation: They recorded the cities and boundaries so Joshua could cast lots and make the allotments before the Lord.

medium.question: What does the phrase 'cast lots' imply in 'Joshua cast lots for them in Shiloh before the Lord'?
answers: A weapon's name
A ritual or impartial method used to decide allotment
A geographic reference
medium.explanation: Casting lots was a method of decision, and doing it 'before the Lord' made it a solemn, divinely acknowledged process.

medium.question: What took place at Shiloh according to these verses?
answers: A new altar was built there
A new religious covenant was made
Joshua cast lots and divided the land among the Israelites there
medium.explanation: The verses say 'Joshua cast lots... in Shiloh: and there Joshua divided the land' — the allotment occurred at Shiloh.

challenge.question: What does 'in a book' mean in the phrase 'described it by cities into seven parts in a book' (context phrase: "in a book")?
answers: Carved on a large stone
Recorded in writing (a scroll or book)
Kept only in oral memory
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates the survey was written down in a book or scroll as a record, not just memory or carving on stone.

challenge.question: What is the religious‑ritual meaning of Joshua 'casting lots... before the Lord'?
answers: That they treated the division as the result of divine will and accepted the lot's outcome as God's decision
That it was a children's game with no significance
That the division was decided by a commercial land sale
challenge.explanation: The wording 'before the Lord' shows the ceremony was religious and the lots' results were regarded as reflecting divine will.

challenge.question: Why did Joshua send the men 'to walk through the land' before the allotment according to the verses' logic?
answers: To check the weather only
To find trees for construction
To map and determine cities and areas so the allotment could be done accurately
challenge.explanation: The walking and recording prepared a map/list of cities and regions necessary for a proper division of the land.

questions.question: What does 'in a book' mean in the phrase 'described it by cities into seven parts in a book' (context phrase: "in a book")?
answers: Carved on a large stone
Recorded in writing (a scroll or book)
Kept only in oral memory
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates the survey was written down in a book or scroll as a record, not just memory or carving on stone.

That it was a children's game with no significance
That the division was decided by a commercial land sale
questions.explanation: The wording 'before the Lord' shows the ceremony was religious and the lots' results were regarded as reflecting divine will.

answers: To check the weather only
To find trees for construction

questions.explanation: The walking and recording prepared a map/list of cities and regions necessary for a proper division of the land.

paragraphs.title: Initial Border of the Tribe of Benjamin

easy.question: Which tribe's lot is described here?
answers: The children of Benjamin
The Levites
The tribe of Dan
easy.explanation: The verse opens 'And the lot of the tribe of the children of Benjamin came up' — it concerns Benjamin.

easy.question: The lot for Benjamin came out between which two tribes?
answers: Between Levi and Ishmael
Between Judah and Joseph
Between Reuben and Simeon
easy.explanation: Verse 11 states the border came 'between the children of Judah and the children of Joseph' — Benjamin lay between them.

easy.question: Up to which city did the border go northward according to the verse?
answers: Bethel
Jerusalem
Jericho
easy.explanation: The verse says the border 'went up to the side of Jericho on the north' — it reached Jericho on the north side.

medium.question: On which side relative to the Jordan was Benjamin's border according to the verse?
answers: To the north side from the Jordan
South of the Jordan
Only west of the Jordan
medium.explanation: The verse notes 'their border on the north side was from Jordan' — meaning the border lay northward relative to the Jordan.

medium.question: What does 'the side of Jericho' mean in 'to the side of Jericho' (context phrase: "to the side of Jericho")?
answers: A summit of a high mountain
The side or edge (the flank) of the place
A river bank
medium.explanation: 'Side' here means the flank or edge of a location; 'to the side of Jericho' indicates the boundary reached the edge of Jericho.

medium.question: What does the fact that Benjamin's border lay 'between Judah and Joseph' suggest about Benjamin's territory?
answers: That it was a small area situated between comparatively larger tribes (Judah and Joseph)
That Benjamin's territory was the largest of all tribes
That Benjamin extended across the Jordan
medium.explanation: Being placed between Judah and Joseph suggests Benjamin had a limited territory bounded by larger neighboring tribes.

challenge.question: How might the phrase 'and went up into the hill country westward' be interpreted geographically?
answers: As if the border descended into an eastern valley
As the border ascending to hills toward the west (the mountains toward the sea)
As the border crossing the sea to the west
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates an ascent to the western hills (toward the sea), i.e., the border rises into the western hill country.

challenge.question: What does this passage let us infer about Benjamin's proximity to the Jordan River?
answers: That it was far from the Jordan and had no contact with it
That the border lay north of Jordan and near Jericho in the Jordan valley
That it sat on the Mediterranean coast
challenge.explanation: Mentions of the border from Jordan and to the side of Jericho show Benjamin's territory reached into the Jordan valley near Jericho.

challenge.question: What does the location 'between Judah and Joseph' imply about Benjamin's strategic position?
answers: It was isolated deep in the desert
It was nestled between powerful neighbors, indicating a central but limited land
It was the frontier beyond Jordan
challenge.explanation: Being between Judah and Joseph shows Benjamin occupied a central but relatively small area surrounded by stronger tribes.

questions.question: How might the phrase 'and went up into the hill country westward' be interpreted geographically?
answers: As if the border descended into an eastern valley
As the border ascending to hills toward the west (the mountains toward the sea)
As the border crossing the sea to the west
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates an ascent to the western hills (toward the sea), i.e., the border rises into the western hill country.

answers: That it was far from the Jordan and had no contact with it
That the border lay north of Jordan and near Jericho in the Jordan valley
That it sat on the Mediterranean coast
questions.explanation: Mentions of the border from Jordan and to the side of Jericho show Benjamin's territory reached into the Jordan valley near Jericho.

questions.question: What does the location 'between Judah and Joseph' imply about Benjamin's strategic position?
answers: It was isolated deep in the desert
It was nestled between powerful neighbors, indicating a central but limited land
It was the frontier beyond Jordan
questions.explanation: Being between Judah and Joseph shows Benjamin occupied a central but relatively small area surrounded by stronger tribes.

easy.question: Which tribe is confirmed as receiving the inheritance at the end of the section?
answers: The children of Benjamin
The children of Judah
The children of Reuben
easy.explanation: Verse 20 explicitly says 'This was the inheritance of the children of Benjamin'.

easy.question: Which river serves as the eastern border in the final verse of this section?
answers: The Mediterranean Sea
The brook Kidron
The Jordan
easy.explanation: Verse 20 states 'And Jordan was the border of it on the east side' — the Jordan River is the eastern boundary.

easy.question: How is Kirjath‑baal (Kirjath‑jearim) described in verse 14?
answers: A seaport
A city of the children of Judah
A spring
easy.explanation: Verse 14 calls Kirjath‑baal 'a city of the children of Judah' — it is a Judahite city.

medium.question: What does the repeated use of 'went down' or 'descended' in the border descriptions suggest?
answers: That the border climbed from the valley into the hills
That the text only lists points without direction
That the border descends from higher hills down toward valleys and the Jordan
medium.explanation: The repetition indicates movement from higher elevations down into valleys toward the Jordan valley.

medium.question: What does 'quarter' mean in the phrase 'this was the west quarter' (context phrase: "this was the west quarter")?
answers: A corner or side of the territory
A mountain range name
A type of spring
medium.explanation: 'Quarter' denotes a side or section of the territory — here the west side.

medium.question: Which spring is mentioned in verse 15 as a boundary point?
answers: The spring of Nephtoah
En‑rogel
Ein Shemesh
medium.explanation: Verse 15 refers to 'the well of waters of Nephtoah' as one of the border points.

challenge.question: Do the verses indicate the border reaches 'the north bay of the salt sea' (the north end of the Dead Sea)?
answers: Yes — the descriptions lead to the north bay of the salt sea
No — there is no reference to the Dead Sea
Yes — but the reference is actually to the Mediterranean coast
challenge.explanation: Verse 19 explicitly states 'the outgoings of the border were at the north bay of the salt sea' — i.e., the north end of the Dead Sea.

challenge.question: What landscape best fits the region described (with 'went down', hills of Beth‑horon, the valley of Ben‑Hinnom, and Jordan)?
answers: A flat sandy plain along a sea coast
An open desert with no hills
A mountain ridge descending into valleys leading to the Jordan valley
challenge.explanation: The text describes descents from hills into valleys and toward the Jordan, indicating a mountainous region falling to the valley.

challenge.question: What is meant by 'the outgoings of the border' in 'the outgoings of the border were at the north bay of the salt sea' (context phrase: "the outgoings of the border")?
answers: The flows of a spring into the sea
The border's endpoints — points where it reaches the bay of the salt sea
People leaving the city
challenge.explanation: In boundary descriptions, 'outgoings' refers to the border's extremities or points where the boundary meets the bay, not water flow or people.

questions.question: Do the verses indicate the border reaches 'the north bay of the salt sea' (the north end of the Dead Sea)?
answers: Yes — the descriptions lead to the north bay of the salt sea
No — there is no reference to the Dead Sea
Yes — but the reference is actually to the Mediterranean coast
questions.explanation: Verse 19 explicitly states 'the outgoings of the border were at the north bay of the salt sea' — i.e., the north end of the Dead Sea.

answers: A flat sandy plain along a sea coast
An open desert with no hills
A mountain ridge descending into valleys leading to the Jordan valley
questions.explanation: The text describes descents from hills into valleys and toward the Jordan, indicating a mountainous region falling to the valley.

questions.question: What is meant by 'the outgoings of the border' in 'the outgoings of the border were at the north bay of the salt sea' (context phrase: "the outgoings of the border")?
answers: The flows of a spring into the sea
The border's endpoints — points where it reaches the bay of the salt sea
People leaving the city
questions.explanation: In boundary descriptions, 'outgoings' refers to the border's extremities or points where the boundary meets the bay, not water flow or people.

easy.question: Which tribe received these cities according to the text?
answers: The children of Benjamin
The children of Judah
The Levites
easy.explanation: The section begins 'The inheritance of the children of Benjamin' — these cities belong to Benjamin.

easy.question: How many cities are listed as Benjamin's in the closing verse of the list?
answers: Twelve
Fourteen
Eighteen
easy.explanation: Verse 28 states 'fourteen cities with their villages' — fourteen cities.

easy.question: Which of these is identified as a Jebusite city in the list?
answers: Zelah
Gibeon
Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The verse says 'Jebusi, which is Jerusalem' — identifying Jerusalem as the Jebusite city.

medium.question: When the text says 'and their villages and their suburbs', what does it indicate?
answers: The list includes the cities and their surrounding villages and yards
It lists only suburbs without the cities
It lists only fortified towns
medium.explanation: The phrase shows the allotment covers the named cities plus their surrounding villages and outlying areas.

medium.question: What does the clause 'which is Jerusalem' tell us about 'Jebusi' (context phrase: "which is Jerusalem")?
answers: It is the name of a nearby mountain
It identifies the Jebusite settlement as Jerusalem
It describes a building type
medium.explanation: The clause clarifies that 'Jebusi' refers to the Jebusite city, which is Jerusalem.

medium.question: Which city from the list appears in verses 25–27?
answers: Shechem
Tyre
Gibeon
medium.explanation: Verses 25–27 include names like Gibeon, Ramah, and Beeroth — Gibeon is listed there.

challenge.question: Why is the note 'which is Jerusalem' historically significant?
answers: Because it shows Jerusalem was still inhabited by Jebusites and not yet conquered by Israel at the time of the allotment
Because it states the city was destroyed
Because it indicates the city was outside the land of Israel
challenge.explanation: Noting 'which is Jerusalem' indicates that at the time of allotment Jerusalem was a Jebusite city and not yet under Israelite control — an important historical detail.

challenge.question: How can the shift from listing twelve cities to 'fourteen' at the end be explained?
answers: It is a copying error in the text
The initial list was partial and later verses add two more cities, totaling fourteen
The numbers refer to different categories entirely
challenge.explanation: The passage first lists part of the cities and continues with additional names; the total at the end is given as fourteen.

challenge.question: Which listed city is located in the central hill country north of Jerusalem and appears in these verses?
answers: Jericho
Bethel
Zemarim
challenge.explanation: Bethel is a known settlement in the central hill country north of Jerusalem and is mentioned among the cities.

answers: Jericho
Bethel
Zemarim
